jobs.description:
Job Description

BAE Systems, Inc. has a contingent opening for an Expert-level Geospatial Analyst supporting US Army INSCOM primarily on Ft. Gordon, GA. The candidate’s role will be to perform GEOINT exploitation, analysis and reporting of all Advanced GEOINT and Full Spectrum GEOINT (FSG) related disciplines, tradecraft, and products produced by INSCOM MIB-Theater Integrated GEOINT Divisions (IGD). Sub-disciplines include but are not limited to Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR), Electro-Optical (EO), Moving Target Indicator (MTI), Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR), Geospatial Information and Services (GI&S), Wide Area Persistent Surveillance (WAPS), geospatial data processing, and general intelligence analysis. The candidate must possess extensive knowledge and experience in GEOINT and be considered an expert in the field.

#GACC

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

MA/MS degree in a technical field such as Geospatial Information & Services (GIS), Geomatics, Geospatial Sciences, or related field AND 10 years of relevant experience;

OR

BA/BS degree in a technical field such as GIS, Geomatics, Geospatial Sciences, or related field AND 15 years of relevant experience.

Relevant experience must be in geospatial analysis and/or geospatial information systems.

Expert knowledge of industry standard location analysis desktop and server applications such as Esri ArcGIS Platform, QGIS, MapBox, GeoServer, etc.

Experience using and managing spatial relational databases including Oracle, MSSQL, or PostGreSQL/PostGIS.

Extensive experience with geographically-derived assessments, enterprise data integration, spatial data governance, metadata management and interpretation of business and performance metrics.

Expert ability to present geospatial information via multimedia presentations and written reports.

Demonstrated experience using geospatial Python, R, SAS, Java or other coding languages to deliver custom geoprocessing and analytical workflows.

Experience in coordination and collaboration with industry counterparts on technical projects, software and service assessment, and other related subject material.

Ability to work non-traditional hours or days if mission requirements emerge.

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills

Experience with Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of War (DoW) geospatial data and repositories; working within common project management frameworks.

Demonstrated knowledge and experience in cartography, GIS, spatial modeling.

Familiarity with Army, DoW, or IC geospatial processes, policy, programs, Structured Observation Management (SOM), and object-based production.

Private sector (e.g., GISP, Esri Professional, etc.) or government (e.g., GPC series) professional GIS certification.

Knowledge of Microsoft office tools and graphic design principles.

Completion of related Army (or service equivalent) 35/350G, 12Y/125D, or 35F/350F military occupational specialty school.

jobs.description:
STV is seeking a GIS Analyst to join our Digital Advisory department in one of our major Texas office locations.

Key Responsibilities

Assist with GIS and data analysis, prepare and execute queries, and produce maps, spreadsheets, graphs, and other analytical products.
Develop and manage interactive web maps, dashboards, and data-driven applications using ArcGIS Online and related tools.
Perform advanced spatial analysis and support data analytics workflows to inform infrastructure planning and decision-making.
Prepare, collect, organize, and input data to maintain and enhance the company's GIS.
Assist with interpreting as-built drawings, construction plans, engineering plans, recorded maps, deeds, legal descriptions, imagery, and other source documents, incorporating them into GIS using various methods, including coordinate geometry (COGO), digitizing, and GPS.
Create and maintain multiple GIS layers, including parcels, streets, right-of-way, floodplain, other development layers, and water and sewer system layers.
Follow quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) processes, performing routine data management tasks such as validation, correction, queries, and editing to ensure GIS data accuracy, integrity, and completeness.
Support subject matter experts in regulatory reporting to meet client mapping standards and templates.
Maintain and update geospatial databases to accurately reflect the location and attributes of utility assets.
Create, edit, and validate utility maps (water, sewer, electric, telecom) using GIS software to support design, planning, and field operations.
Incorporate field-collected data (GPS, survey, SUE) and as-built drawings into GIS systems, ensuring alignment with existing records and standards.
Create custom maps that are cartographically sound, visually engaging, and effectively communicate complex spatial information to diverse audiences.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, GIS&T, Geography, or a closely related field.
0.9-3 years of professional GIS experience.
Proficiency with the ESRI suite of GIS software, including ArcMap and ArcGIS Pro.
Strong experience with ArcGIS Online products, including Web AppBuilder, Experience Builder, and Dashboards.
Familiarity with open-source GIS software.
Experience with data visualization and geospatial data analytics.
Strong attention to detail and data integrity, with the ability to perform QA/QC.
Excellent communication and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of more than one million contributors from diverse backgrounds who help customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and contribute to the development of innovative AI technologies used by some of the world's largest brands.
Millions of people rely on digital maps every day to navigate, to discover, to find their way. But maps are only as accurate as the data behind them, and data is only as trustworthy as the people who verify it. Your knowledge of USA's geography, local landmarks, and how people actually navigate your region is something no algorithm can fully replicate. That local intelligence is what makes maps genuinely useful.

A Day in the Life of an Online Data Analyst

In this role, you will conduct structured quality audits on spatial and mapping datasets. Your role is to verify, evaluate, and validate complex geographic and business information using advanced mapping tools and detailed reference materials.

Conduct structured quality audits on spatial datasets using mapping platforms, search directories, and GIS-standard evaluation tools
Evaluate and cross-reference complex business, geographic, and cultural data entries against multiple authoritative sources
Perform root-cause analysis when spatial data points conflict across sources, documenting the discrepancy with precise reasoning
Apply detailed evaluation frameworks with consistency and rigor across dozens of geographic, business, and cultural data variations
Be open to work across a diverse set of Task Types (e.g. Maps, News, Audio tasks, Relevance)
Provide structured feedback that helps refine mapping algorithms and improve geographic intelligence

Why this matters:
Accurately verified mapping data prevents real-world navigation errors. Your verification work ensures people can reliably find critical services, reach trusted businesses, and navigate with confidence. At scale, this is infrastructure work that is foundational to how billions of people interact with geographic information.

Why join the project:

Fully remote flexibility:
Complete work from anywhere with stable internet, structuring your schedule around academic research, consulting, or other professional commitments
Structured onboarding:
Access comprehensive evaluation guidelines, detailed reference materials, and practical examples before your first live assessment
Direct feedback and growth:
Receive performance assessments tied to quality metrics so you can refine your evaluation precision

Each evaluation requires methodical reasoning, framework interpretation, and structured discrepancy analysis.

Professional fluency in English and Spanish (native or near-native proficiency required)

Advanced analytical thinking and methodical problem-solving ability
Deep regional, cultural, and geographic knowledge of USA
Comfort with rigorous guideline interpretation and consistent framework application
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience in analytical, technical, or research disciplines (strongly preferred)
Stable internet connection and access to a personal computer

Who You Are  

You are a highly organized, detail-oriented project professional who enjoys bringing structure, clarity, and follow-through to complex work. You are comfortable coordinating multiple priorities, maintaining accurate project information, communicating with a variety of stakeholders, and identifying issues before they become larger problems. You take ownership of your commitments, learn quickly, and bring a collaborative, client-focused mindset to every interaction.  
About The Role  

As a Project Coordinator within the Project Management Office (PMO), you will support Project Managers and Program Managers in the planning, coordination, tracking, and successful delivery of client-facing technology projects. You will help maintain accurate project schedules, documentation, action items, risks, dependencies, financial information, and status reporting so project teams and stakeholders have timely visibility into progress and emerging concerns. This role is well suited for someone who can balance detail-oriented administrative execution with proactive communication, sound judgment, and a desire to grow within project management.  
Must be based in the United States of America.
The role may support multiple projects, clients, and internal teams simultaneously and may occasionally coordinate with stakeholders across different time zones.  
Other responsibilities include:

Support Project Managers and Program Managers with project planning, coordination, tracking, and follow-through from initiation through closeout.  

Maintain accurate project schedules, milestones, deliverables, action items, decision logs, risk registers, dependency trackers, and other project controls.  

Coordinate project meetings, prepare agendas and materials, capture notes and decisions, distribute follow-up actions, and monitor completion.  

Prepare recurring project status updates, dashboards, and health reports using current and validated project information.  

Track project progress against scope, schedule, budget, resource plans, and key client commitments; escalate variances and emerging risks promptly.  

Coordinate information and handoffs among Project Management, Program Management, Solutions Architecture, Engineering, Logistics, Finance, vendors, subcontractors, and client stakeholders.  

Support project financial administration, including purchase-order and invoice status, time and expense tracking, budget updates, cost documentation, and forecast inputs as assigned.

Assist with resource coordination, onboarding activities, site or field-readiness documentation, logistics tracking, and project communications as needed.  

Proactively identify missing information, schedule conflicts, unresolved decisions, and delivery risks; research issues and coordinate resolution with the appropriate owners.

Contribute to continuous improvement of PMO templates, reporting standards, workflows, and project coordination practices.

Strong organizational and time-management skills with exceptional attention to detail and consistent follow-through.  

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate professionally with clients, vendors, subcontractors, and internal teams.

As a Project Coordinator within the Project Management Office (PMO), you will support Project Managers and Program Managers in the planning, coordination, tracking, and successful delivery of client-facing technology projects.
